collection_method: Read-only GitHub issue search and issue/comment GET requests through the GitHub connector. Embedded snippets were treated as evidence and not executed. No attachments, linked demonstrations or code files, packages, agent runtimes, reproduction steps, target systems, or external tools were opened or run.

selected_records.title: Long tool calls (~180s+) silently re-executed from checkpoint on LangGraph Cloud
selected_records.provider_attribution: Reporter-attributed to managed LangGraph Cloud and deepagents SubAgentMiddleware; no model provider was stated or independently verified.
selected_records.assessment: The reporter describes main-agent task dispatch to subagents, checkpoint redispatch after roughly three minutes without a new model decision, and two or three copies completing. Identical arguments and separate tool nodes are concrete execution evidence as reported, while the open issue and later comments do not prove continuing runs. This is a previously public hierarchical retry/idempotency incident with unauthorized duplicate work and cost, not independent rogue coordination.

selected_records.title: Sub Agent sends back to starting agent after handoff even if it is waiting on further responses to finish it task from user
selected_records.provider_attribution: Reporter-configured LangGraph handoff workflow; model/provider details in embedded examples are not independent provenance.
selected_records.assessment: A designed mediator-to-subagent workflow reportedly loses pending ownership across user turns and starts again at the mediator. Public replies frame this as missing interrupt or active-agent state. It is a handoff-state failure, not an unauthorized peer exchange.

selected_records.title: Interrupt resume values misrouted between tools when using a ToolNode
selected_records.provider_attribution: LangGraph ToolNode interrupt routing; no autonomous-agent or model-provider attribution.
selected_records.assessment: A bounded parallel-tool reproduction reports resume values sharing an interrupt identity and reaching the wrong tool path. A collaborator recommended separate Send tasks and the issue closed. This is a tool-resume routing control, not distinct agents exchanging results.

selected_records.title: Bug: PUSH child task deduplication fails on parent retry
selected_records.provider_attribution: LangGraph runner logic; no model provider or autonomous participant attribution.
selected_records.assessment: The issue supplies a synthetic runner-level reproduction in which a retried parent admits a second child object with the same logical task ID. Later public comments claim the regression remained on a then-current main branch, but this collection did not execute it. It is a duplicate-admission control, not a documented agent exchange.

selected_records.title: EncryptedSerializer AEAD has no associated-data binding
selected_records.provider_attribution: LangGraph encrypted checkpoint design; no model provider attribution.
selected_records.assessment: The report identifies a design gap that could let a store-level writer replay valid ciphertext into a different thread/checkpoint position. It describes a preconditioned attack possibility, not an observed agent action or coordination episode.

novelty_result: No previously unreported rogue swarm confirmed. The production-shaped duplicate-subagent report was already public and describes retry behavior inside an operator-configured hierarchy; the remaining records are designed handoff failures, tool routing, synthetic duplicate admission, or a potential checkpoint attack.
limitations: Searches were capped at 30 newest-updated rows and overlap heavily; this is not a repository census.
Issue text and comments are reporter assertions, not authenticated execution telemetry.
Many comments on issue 7417 are third-party workarounds or product promotions; they do not independently verify the original run.
Open issue state and recent comments do not establish ongoing autonomous activity.
No attachments, external reproductions, packages, linked code files, agent runtimes, or linked target systems were opened or executed; embedded issue snippets were not run.

Advancement requires a not-previously-published original exchange with independently corroborated autonomous participants, actual result transfer and recipient use, and evidence that the coordination—not only scheduler replay, retry, state loss or a synthetic test—exceeded operator authorization.
redactions: No payload bodies, credentials, personal addresses, sink identifiers, tokens, or private logs are included.
Assessments summarize incident shape without reproducing executable demonstrations or tool-call content.
